Silver nanoparticles were synthesized by chemical reduction using glucose as a reducing agent, producing particles sized 1-100 nm.
Huntite/hydromagnesite minerals serve as non-halogenated flame retardants in the composite.
Barium hexaferrite particles were prepared by citrate sol–gel method and provide radar absorbing properties.
Chitosan with molecular weight 150 kDa and 84.5% degree of deacetylation was used for self-healing.
Epoxy dye matrix is a thermosetting copolymer formed from epichlorohydrin and bisphenol-A resin with polyamine hardener.

Composite samples were prepared with varying additive loadings, e.g., silver nanoparticles from 0 to 0.2%, huntite/hydromagnesite from 10 to 30%, barium hexaferrite from 0 to 20%, chitosan from 0.01 to 0.2%.
Antibacterial activity was tested against S. aureus and E. coli using agar diffusion, showing inhibition zones correlated with silver content.
Flame retardancy was evaluated by Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI) and UL94 tests to measure combustion resistance.
Radar absorbing properties were imparted by barium hexaferrite particles, confirmed by magnetic characterization.
Self-healing was enabled by chitosan's reversible cross-linking activated by UV light and mechanical damage.
FTIR, SEM-EDS, and XRD analyses confirmed the presence and distribution of additives within the epoxy matrix.
Adhesion strength of coatings was measured by scratch testing and converted to MPa using hardness conversion tables.
Surface roughness and morphology of coatings were characterized by surface profilometry and SEM imaging.
The multifunctional composite coatings were applied on plastic, glass, and metal substrates.
Synergistic effects of the additives resulted in enhanced multifunctional performance without compromising individual properties.
